heroHeadline: Oreshnik IRBM Strikes Bila Tserkva as Russia Launches Largest Kyiv Attack Since 2022 — 600 Drones + 90 Missiles; National Chernobyl Museum Destroyed
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,550, Russia fired an RS-26 'Oreshnik' intermediate-range ballistic missile at Bila Tserkva, Kyiv Oblast — a city of 200,000 people 64 km from Kyiv — in the largest aerial assault on the Ukrainian capital since the war began, combining 600 drones and 90 missiles. Ukraine intercepted 604 of 690 projectiles; 51 drones and 16 missiles struck 54 locations, killing 1–2 and injuring 77–83 people. The National Chernobyl Museum (Podil, Kyiv) was nearly completely destroyed, along with the National Philharmonic, Music Academy, National Library, Kyiv Opera, and four other cultural institutions. Russia framed the attack as retaliation for Ukraine's May 22 Starobilsk strike. The preceding day (May 23), Ukraine struck Russia's Sheskharis oil terminal and Grushovaya depot in Novorossiysk — Russia's largest Black Sea crude export hub (~20% of total exports) — setting both facilities ablaze. Simultaneously, Ukrainian forces conducted 173 combat engagements on May 23, launching a Borova counterattack that recaptured Odradne (~22 km²). A large prisoner exchange (1,000/side) began May 23 from the Istanbul talks, even as diplomacy collapsed: Russia rejected the Vatican as a new venue, with Lavrov calling it 'unrealistic.' Russian cumulative losses reached ~1,355,920 personnel as of May 24 — Day 1,550 — with the UN Security Council convening to note the war is 'becoming deadlier by the day.'
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, France 24, NPR, CNN, NBC News, PBS, The Moscow Times, CGTN, Newsweek, Yahoo News, Kyiv Post, Euromaidan Press, EMPR Media, CNBC, Semafor, CBC, and Euronews. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
